[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"Prove that, ∠ACD = ∠BAC + ∠ABC.","marks":0,"answer":"Proof:
- Extend side BC of △ABC to D to produce exterior ∠ACD.
- Draw CP ray through C parallel to BA.
- BA ∥ CP and AC is the transversal ⇒ ∠BAC = ∠ACP (alternate angles) … (i)
- BA ∥ CP and BD is transversal ⇒ ∠ABC = ∠PCD (corresponding angles) … (ii)
- Adding (i) and (ii): ∠BAC + ∠ABC = ∠ACP + ∠PCD = ∠ACD
- ∴ ∠ACD = ∠BAC + ∠ABC (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142556900_y619ge.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142556900_y619ge.jpeg"},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Prove that, ∠ACD + ∠ABE > 2 right angles.","marks":0,"answer":"Proof:
- In △ABC, exterior ∠ABE = ∠A + ∠C … (i)
- Exterior ∠ACD = ∠A + ∠B … (ii)
- Adding (i) and (ii): ∠ABE + ∠ACD = ∠A + ∠B + ∠C + ∠A = 180° + ∠A
- Since ∠A > 0°, ∠ABE + ∠ACD > 180°
- ∴ ∠ACD + ∠ABE > 2 right angles (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142556900_cs7uoe.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142556900_cs7uoe.jpeg"},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"If F is the midpoint of BC, then prove that, AB + AC > 2AF.","marks":0,"answer":"Proof:
- F is midpoint of BC. Join A and F. Extend AF to P such that FP = AF. Join P and C.
- In △ABF and △PCF:
BF = CF (F is midpoint)
AF = PF (construction)
∠AFB = ∠PFC (vertically opposite)
∴ △ABF ≅ △PCF ⇒ AB = CP … (i)
- In △APC: AC + CP > AP (sum of two sides > third side)
⇒ AC + AB > AF + PF
⇒ AB + AC > AF + AF (since PF = AF)
∴ AB + AC > 2AF (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142556900_6pmbno.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142556900_6pmbno.jpeg"}]

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"If the length of a median of an equilateral triangle is 3 cm, determine the length of one side.","marks":0,"answer":"Let side of equilateral △ABC = a cm, median AD = 3 cm.
In right △ABD:
\[
AB^2 = BD^2 + AD^2 \Rightarrow a^2 = \left(\frac{a}{2}\right)^2 + 3^2 \Rightarrow a^2 - \frac{a^2}{4} = 9 \Rightarrow \frac{3a^2}{4} = 9 \Rightarrow a^2 = 12
\]
∴ \(a = \sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}\) cm.
Alternative:
Height of equilateral triangle = \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} a\)
Given median = height = 3 cm:
\[
\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} a = 3 \Rightarrow a = \frac{6}{\sqrt{3}} = 2\sqrt{3} \text{ cm}
\]
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142556901_0jq40l.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142556901_0jq40l.jpeg"},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Prove that, AD + BE + CF < AB + BC + AC.","marks":0,"answer":"Proof:
- Extend AD to G such that DG = AD. Join G, C.
- In △ABD and △GCD:
BD = CD (D midpoint), AD = GD, ∠ADB = ∠GDC (vertically opposite)
∴ △ABD ≅ △GCD ⇒ AB = CG … (i)
- In △ACG: AC + CG > AG ⇒ AC + AB > AD + GD ⇒ AB + AC > 2AD … (ii)
- Similarly: BC + AB > 2BE … (iii) and CA + BC > 2CF … (iv)
- Adding (ii), (iii), (iv):
\(2(AB + BC + CA) > 2(AD + BE + CF)\)
⇒ \(AB + BC + CA > AD + BE + CF\)
∴ \(AD + BE + CF < AB + BC + AC\) (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142556901_c3o1lb.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142556901_c3o1lb.jpeg"},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"If AP is the bisector of ∠A, prove that ∠APB is obtuse.","marks":0,"answer":"Proof:
- In △ABC, AB > AC ⇒ ∠C > ∠B.
- Add \(\frac{1}{2}∠A\) to both sides: \(\angle C + \frac{1}{2}\angle A > \angle B + \frac{1}{2}\angle A\)
- In △ACP: exterior ∠APB = ∠C + \(\frac{1}{2}∠A\)
- In △ABP: exterior ∠APC = ∠B + \(\frac{1}{2}∠A\)
- Since ∠C + \(\frac{1}{2}∠A\) > ∠B + \(\frac{1}{2}∠A\), we have ∠APB > ∠APC.
- ∠APB and ∠APC are adjacent supplementary angles, so ∠APB > 90° ⇒ obtuse (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142556901_zx0kzp.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142556901_zx0kzp.jpeg"}]

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"If the area of a circle is 100 sq. cm, determine its radius.","marks":0,"answer":"Area of circle = πr² = 100
\[
r^2 = \frac{100}{\pi} \approx \frac{100}{3.1416} \approx 31.83 \Rightarrow r \approx 5.642 \text{ cm}
\]
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"If M and N are midpoints of AB and AC, prove that MN ∥ BC.","marks":0,"answer":"Proof:
- Join M and N, extend MN to F such that MN = NF. Join C, F.
- In △AMN and △CNF:
AN = NC (N midpoint), MN = NF, ∠ANM = ∠CNF (vertically opposite)
∴ △AMN ≅ △CNF ⇒ ∠AMN = ∠NFC, ∠MAN = ∠NCF
⇒ AM ∥ CF ⇒ AB ∥ CF
- But BM = AM = CF and BM ∥ CF ⇒ BMFC is a parallelogram ⇒ MF ∥ BC
∴ MN ∥ BC (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142558486_ox42a8.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142558486_ox42a8.jpeg"},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"If bisector of ∠A meets BC at P, prove that ∠APC is acute.","marks":0,"answer":"Proof:
- In △ABC, AB > AC ⇒ ∠C > ∠B
⇒ ∠C + \(\frac{1}{2}∠A\) > ∠B + \(\frac{1}{2}∠A\)
- In △ACP: exterior ∠APB = ∠C + \(\frac{1}{2}∠A\)
- In △ABP: exterior ∠APC = ∠B + \(\frac{1}{2}∠A\)
- Since ∠C + \(\frac{1}{2}∠A\) > ∠B + \(\frac{1}{2}∠A\), ∠APB > ∠APC
- ∠APB and ∠APC are adjacent supplementary ⇒ ∠APC < 90° ⇒ acute (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142558486_uhpv63.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142558486_uhpv63.jpeg"}]

- E and F are midpoints of AB and AC. Join E and F, extend EF to G such that FG = EF. Join C, G.
- In △AEF and △CGF:
AF = FC, EF = FG, ∠AFE = ∠CFG (vertically opposite)
∴ △AEF ≅ △CGF ⇒ ∠AEF = ∠FGC, ∠EAF = ∠GCF ⇒ AE ∥ CG ⇒ AB ∥ CG
- BE = AE = CG and BE ∥ CG ⇒ BEGC is a parallelogram ⇒ EG ∥ BC ⇒ EF ∥ BC
- Also EG = BC ⇒ EF + FG = BC ⇒ 2EF = BC ⇒ EF = ½ BC (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142556901_qxxvy5.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142556901_qxxvy5.jpeg"},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Prove that AD + BF + CE < AB + BC + AC.","marks":0,"answer":"This is identical to Question 2(b).
Proof:
- By extending each median similarly, we get:
AB + AC > 2AD
BC + AB > 2BE
CA + BC > 2CF
- Adding: 2(AB + BC + CA) > 2(AD + BE + CF)
⇒ AB + BC + CA > AD + BE + CF
∴ AD + BF + CE < AB + BC + AC (Proved)
","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts:
[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"If ∠PNR = 55° and MN = MO, find ∠NMO.","marks":0,"answer":"Given ∠PNR = ∠ONR = 55°, MN = MO ⇒ △MNO is isosceles.
∠PNO = ∠PNR + ∠ONR = 55° + 55° = 110°
∠MNO = 180° − ∠PNO = 180° − 110° = 70° (linear pair)
Since MN = MO (isosceles), ∠MNO = ∠MON = 70°
In △MNO: ∠NMO + ∠MNO + ∠MON = 180°
⇒ ∠NMO + 70° + 70° = 180°
⇒ ∠NMO = 40°
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Prove that MN + MO > 2MD.","marks":0,"answer":"Proof:
- In △MON, D is midpoint of NO (since ND = OD).
- Extend MD to E such that MD = DE. Join O, E.
- In △MDN and △EDO:
ND = OD, MD = DE, ∠MDN = ∠EDO (vertically opposite)
∴ △MDN ≅ △EDO ⇒ MN = OE
- In △MOE: MO + OE > ME ⇒ MO + MN > MD + DE ⇒ MO + MN > 2MD
∴ MN + MO > 2MD (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142558476_77vdm2.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142558476_77vdm2.jpeg"},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Prove that 2∠NRO + ∠NMO = 180°.","marks":0,"answer":"Proof:
- In △MNO: ∠M + ∠N + ∠O = 180° ⇒ ½∠M + ½∠N + ½∠O = 90°
⇒ ½∠N + ½∠O = 90° − ½∠M … (i)
- In △NRO: ∠NRO + ∠RNO + ∠RON = 180°
But ∠RNO = ½∠MNO, ∠RON = ½∠MON (since NR and OR are bisectors)
⇒ ∠NRO + ½∠MNO + ½∠MON = 180°
⇒ ∠NRO + ½(∠MNO + ∠MON) = 180°
⇒ ∠NRO = 180° − ½(∠MNO + ∠MON)
From △MNO: ∠MNO + ∠MON = 180° − ∠M
⇒ ∠NRO = 180° − ½(180° − ∠M) = 180° − 90° + ½∠M = 90° + ½∠M
⇒ 2∠NRO = 180° + ∠M
This doesn't match the required result. Let me reconsider.
Actually, from (i): ½∠N + ½∠O = 90° − ½∠M
In △NRO: ∠NRO = 180° − (½∠N + ½∠O) = 180° − (90° − ½∠M) = 90° + ½∠M
⇒ 2∠NRO = 180° + ∠M
⇒ 2∠NRO + ∠NMO = 180° + ∠M − ∠M = 180°
Wait, this is incorrect. The problem states ∠PNR = ∠ONR and ∠QOR = ∠NOR, meaning NR bisects ∠PNO and OR bisects ∠QON. But ∠PNO is exterior, so ∠RNO = ½(180° − ∠MNO). Let me recalculate:
∠RNO = ½∠PNO = ½(180° − ∠MNO) = 90° − ½∠MNO
∠RON = ½∠QON = ½(180° − ∠MON) = 90° − ½∠MON
In △NRO: ∠NRO + (90° − ½∠MNO) + (90° − ½∠MON) = 180°
⇒ ∠NRO = 180° − 180° + ½(∠MNO + ∠MON)
⇒ ∠NRO = ½(∠MNO + ∠MON) = ½(180° − ∠NMO) = 90° − ½∠NMO
⇒ 2∠NRO = 180° − ∠NMO
∴ 2∠NRO + ∠NMO = 180° (Proved)","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142558477_wvb3aq.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768142558477_wvb3aq.jpeg"}]

- This is identical to Question 1(c) and Question 12(b).

- In △QOR: ∠QOR + ∠OQR + ∠ORQ = 180°

⇒ ∠QOR = ½(∠PQR + ∠PRQ)
- In △PQR: ∠PQR + ∠PRQ = 180° − ∠QPR
⇒ ∠QOR = ½(180° − ∠QPR)
⇒ 2∠QOR = 180° − ∠QPR (Proved)

","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"If AB and AC are extended to E and F respectively, then the bisectors of ∠EBC and ∠FCB meet at O′, prove that ∠BO′C = 90° − ½∠A.","marks":0,"answer":"Proof: (Identical to Question 8(c))
- In △BO′C:
∠BO′C = 180° − [½∠EBC + ½∠FCB]
= 180° − [½(180° − ∠B) + ½(180° − ∠C)]
= 180° − [180° − ½(∠B + ∠C)]
= ½(∠B + ∠C)
- But ½(∠B + ∠C) = ½(180° − ∠A) = 90° − ½∠A
∴ ∠BO′C = 90° − ½∠A (Proved)
